AT FIVE AM I woke to the sound of an explosion 5 meters from my room at an airbnb

I look outside the window and see nothing but smoke billowing

my immediate reaction was that some freak accident happened, and I made my girlfriend get away from the window

She started shaking because a second equally loud sound followed immediately after shaking the house and she was scared

I also heard the little girls in another family staying in this airbnb screaming

Keep in mind, I’ve been in the Army before so I’m very familiar with loud noises (C4, artillery, mortars, you name it)

I assure you this was abnormally loud

Anyways… turns out it was the owner of the airbnb next door celebrating their 40th Birthday. They fired a crudely built cannon stuffed to brim with fireworks (basically a homemade bomb)

Apparently a traditional prank in Italy

5 meters from our window

I think we're close to another NFT gold rush, not necessarily for traders but for teams.

The fact that as a new project you can make seven figures in mint revenue by spending a couple thousand bucks on art, smart contracts etc is just way too attractive.

Especially when it comes to IP-based projects, a category that has been down-only in terms of floor prices and allows new teams to delay meaningful development for years.

And not even talking about established artists like ACK here where it is at least kinda justified.

Big extraction, but people will still mint because they might be able to flip for a couple bucks in profit before it goes to zero.

I'm very comfy in Bitcoin and gold, in the current environment I think they will outperform most other assets and my entry on both of them is solid.

If they reach new ATHs this cycle (or maybe go even higher), I'll be set and would consider this cycle a success. Everything else is just a bonus or a distraction, depending on how it goes.

That being said, I still have high hopes for one or two airdrops and maybe a new fun meta that isn't memecoins, but even if they don't happen I think I'd be happy with my current exposure.
